data.title: Oil Futures Extend Decline on Supply Surplus Expectations — Market Talk
data.description: Crude futures settled lower with the market continuing to focus more on abundant supply than on conflict in the Middle East. While recovering Middle East supply keeps crude under pressure, recent attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz and renewed strikes on Gulf infrastructure "highlight the fragility of this recovery," Sparta Commodities senior oil analyst Abhishek Kumar says in a note. Russian refining is still disrupted by Ukrainian attacks, with crude exports rising as refinery outages limit domestic processing, he adds. "These developments continue to support a geopolitical premium in European diesel despite the broader weakness in crude." Front-month Brent settles down 1.3% at $91.95 a barrel and WTI falls 3.2% to $83.26. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)

Revenue increased by $0.5 million, or 19%, compared to the same period last year. The increase reflects greater tipping fee revenue from higher volumes at the organic waste and composting facilities and stronger RNG output at the Fraser Valley Biogas (“FVB”) and Grow the Energy Circle (“GrowTEC”) facilities.

The net loss decreased by $0.4 million, or 40%, compared to the same period last year, driven by revenue growth, absence of loss on sale of assets, partially offset by higher general and administrative expenses.

Adjusted EBITDA increased by $0.5 million, or 99%, year over year, supported by higher tipping volumes at the organic waste and composting facilities and greater RNG production and related revenue at FVB and GrowTEC.

RNG output reached 56,064 GJ, an increase of 8% over Q3 2025, as the FVB and GrowTEC RNG facilities continued to operate at more stable levels.

Subsequent Events

Subsequent to quarter-end, Farm Credit Canada (“FCC”) expanded its existing project-level credit facility at the Company’s Fraser Valley Biogas facility by $0.8 million. The additional funding will finance near-term optimization at FVB, with the replacement of the facility’s thermal oxidizer, a part of the biogas upgrading process, with a new, more energy-efficient unit.

The upgrade has a total estimated capital cost of approximately $1.4 million, to be funded by a combination of proceeds from this FCC facility increase and operating cash flow. EverGen anticipates partially offsetting these costs by applying for rebates under FortisBC’s Custom Efficiency Program once the upgrade is complete and the actual energy savings are confirmed. The new unit is targeted to be operational by mid-2027. With FVB and GrowTEC continuing to set new RNG production records, the upgrade is expected to further improve efficiency at FVB and support stronger cash flow from EverGen’s core operating assets.

Management Commentary

“Our third-quarter results show our operating improvements continuing to pay off, with higher RNG output and growing feedstock volumes,” said Chase Edgelow, Co-founder and CEO of EverGen.

“With our core assets performing steadily and the Pacific Coast Renewables RNG expansion progressing towards a final investment decision, we remain focused on disciplined capital allocation and accretive growth across both our existing development pipeline and selective inorganic opportunities.

“The increased FCC facility supports a short-payback optimization project at FVB that we expect will improve energy efficiency and cash generation once complete. Pairing low-cost, non-dilutive project-level debt with available grants and incentives is a repeatable playbook we can apply to growth and optimization across the portfolio.”

Complete details of the quarter’s results are available in the Company’s Consolidated Financial Statements and Management’s Discussion and Analysis, which can be found on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the EverGen website at www.evergeninfra.com.

Chief Executive Officer Chase Edgelow and Chief Financial Officer Maria O’Sullivan will host a conference call to discuss the third-quarter results and provide a corporate update on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. ET.

data.title: Nasdaq Regains Ground Despite Nvidia Slump But Dow Tumbles To Five-Month Closing Low
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After trending lower over the past several sessions, stocks turned in a relatively lackluster performance during trading on Wednesday. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 spent much of the day lingering near the unchanged line, although the narrower Dow showed a notable move to the downside.

The major averages eventually ended the day mixed. While the Nasdaq climbed 101.50 points or 0.4 percent to 24,429.88, the S&P 500 dipped 16.90 points or 0.2 percent to a three-month closing low of 7,323.63.

The Dow slumped 561.25 points or 1.1 percent to 50,198.17, hitting its lowest closing level in five months amid a 10.2 percent nosedive by shares of UnitedHealth (UNH).

The choppy trading on Wall Street came as traders digested highly anticipated earnings news from AI giant and market leader Nvidia (NVDA).

After seeing pre-market strength, shares of Nvidia tumbled by 2.9 percent to their lowest closing level in over a year even though the company reported better than expected fiscal third quarter results and raised its revenue guidance.

'Elements of the company's results clearly haven't stood up to greater scrutiny despite upgraded guidance and better-than-expected numbers,' said AJ Bell head of markets Dan Coatsworth. 'While revenues are continuing to grow at pace, there is clearly some concern about how this growth is being financed and how it is converting into profit and cash flow.'

He added, 'Investors are less minded to give the business the benefit of the doubt in the wake of the messy departure of former CEO Jensen Huang, and the shares are now on the verge of testing 52-week lows once more.

Traders may also have been reluctant to make more significant moves ahead of Claude developer Anthropic's initial public offering later this week.

'Anthropic offers the next test of appetite with its IPO is expected to be priced today, ahead of an anticipated Nasdaq debut tomorrow,' said Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com.

'Strong demand and a firm first day of trading would suggest investors remain willing to back AI growth, even if they are becoming more selective,' she added. 'A weak reception would add weight to concerns that expectations across the sector have run ahead of what investors are prepared to pay.'

Sector News

Despite the lackluster performance by the broader markets, gold stocks showed a substantial move to the downside amid a steep drop by the price of the precious metal.

With U.S. gold futures plunging by 3.5 percent to their lowest levels in a year, the NYSE Arca Gold Bugs Index nosedived by 5.6 percent to a three-month closing low.

A significant decrease by the price of crude oil also weighed on oil producer stocks, with the NYSE Arca Oil Index plummeting by 4.3 percent.

Pharmaceutical, healthcare and banking stocks also saw considerable weakness, while networking and retail stocks showed strong moves to the upside.

Other Markets

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region turned in a mixed performance during trading on Wednesday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index rose by 0.3 percent, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index slid by 0.9 percent.

Meanwhile, the major European markets all moved to the downside on the day. While the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index tumbled by 1.3 percent, the German DAX Index slumped by 1.2 percent and the French CAC 40 Index declined by 0.9 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries have extended the upward move seen over the two previous sessions. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, has fallen 3.5 basis points to 5.068 percent.

data.description:

Net interest income increased 18% through the first nine months of the year, while core net interest margin expanded by 15 basis points during the quarter to 4.02%. Our payments business is also generating meaningful fee income growth, with payment card and service charge income up 22% through the first nine months of the year. Quarterly noninterest expense declined below $30 million, reflecting continued expense discipline. data.title: Granite Awarded Groundwater Replenishment Project in Coachella Valley
data.description:
Granite () announced today that it has been awarded the Whitewater River Channel & Palm Desert Groundwater Replenishment project by the Coachella Valley Water District (CVWD). The contract is valued at approximately $26 million and will be included in Granite’s fourth quarter 2026 CAP.

Granite’s scope of work includes the construction of a wetlands habitat near the North Shore of the Salton Sea along with concrete slope protection, and groundwater replenishment ponds in the Whitewater Channel located in the City of Palm Desert. These ponds will connect to CVWD's Non-Potable Water Pipeline (NPW) system, allowing un-allocated recycled water to percolate into the ground and recharge the underlying aquifer.

The project will expand CVWD’s groundwater replenishment infrastructure to support a reliable, sustainable water supply across the Coachella Valley, while addressing groundwater depletion and providing flood protection.

“This project strengthens Granite's home market strategy by building on our longstanding relationship with CVWD and leveraging our local resources and expertise,” said Granite Regional Vice President Bill Moore. “As habitat restoration continues around the Salton Sea, this work will build on Granite’s established capabilities and reinforce its long-term commitment to environmental restoration and infrastructure in the region.”

Construction is expected to begin in January 2027 and is anticipated to be completed in February 2028.

About Granite

Granite is America’s Infrastructure Company™. Incorporated since 1922, Granite () is one of the largest diversified construction and construction materials companies in the United States as well as a full-suite civil construction provider. Granite’s Code of Conduct and strong Core Values guide the Company and its employees to uphold the highest ethical standards. Granite is an industry leader in safety and an award-winning firm in quality and sustainability. For more information, visit the Granite website, graniteconstruction.com, and connect with Granite on LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram.

data.title: Alberta unveils data center limits, drops oil sands emissions cap
data.description:
By Amanda Stephenson

Canada's main energy-producing province announced new legislation on Wednesday aimed at enhancing protections for communities and landowners while still encouraging data center development and oil and gas growth.

  • The Alberta government said it will restrict data centers 10 megawatts or larger from being built within 600 meters (1,968 feet) of the nearest home, on Alberta’s highest-quality farmland, or on land that is being irrigated. Alberta will also develop a province-wide water-use standard aimed at reducing water consumption by data centers.

  • Alberta's Technology Minister Nate Glubish has been courting Silicon Valley tech giants in an effort to convince them to build large-scale data centers in the province.

  • The legislation will also require energy companies to set aside financial security for the eventual closure and reclamation of any new oil or gas wells drilled. Companies will be required to build up security tied to each new well over time in an effort to reduce strain on Alberta's chronically underfunded orphan well cleanup program.

  • Alberta will eliminate its existing cap on oil sands emissions, which dates from 2016 but has never been enforced. The cap set a 100 million metric tonne limit on greenhouse gas emissions from all Alberta oil sands sites, and was part of former Premier Rachel Notley's climate plan.

  • Oil sands emissions have remained well below the limit set by the cap. Greenhouse gas emissions from the oil sands were approximately 84 million metric tonnes in 2023, according to federal data.

  • Alberta says the oil sands emissions cap is redundant because the province's industrial carbon pricing system already provides an incentive for companies to reduce their greenhouse gas output.

  • Alberta's ruling United Conservative Party has a majority in the provincial legislature.

data.description:
By Rob Curran

U.S. stocks were mixed ahead of Anthropic's initial public offering as Nvidia's efforts to draw a line under the Jensen Huang scandal proved insufficient to stabilize its stock or quell fears about its "neocloud" customers.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 561.25 points, or 1.11%, to 50198.17. The broad S&P 500 slipped 16.90 points, or 0.23%, to 7323.63, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite gained 101.50 points, or 0.42%, to 24429.88.

Nvidia shares fell 2.9% to $150.96. During Tuesday's conference call, Interim Chief Executive Colette Kress pointed to rising chip demand as a sign that it was "business as usual" at the AI bellwether. She failed to allay investor doubts about the trajectory of the company and the tech sector as a whole in the absence of Huang, one of the driving forces behind AI.

Shares of some Nvidia partners, including CoreWeave, fell in the wake of the executive conference call. CoreWeave purchases graphics processing units from Nvidia so that it can stand up data centers and build a "cloud infrastructure" for AI companies. Nvidia also owns a stake in CoreWeave, which lost 4.1% to $47.83. One brokerage said Kress seemed to give the company wiggle room on plans to backstop data-center developers.

"Amidst questions of ecosystem support, Kress outlined on the call that support would remain 'disciplined and selective,' emphasizing closer counterparty scrutiny and identifying land, power and [data-center buildings] as 'the most important part of the financing that [they] would probably review,'" said credit strategists at brokerage Morgan Stanley, in a note to clients. "Tenant quality - or a credible…backstop - appears increasingly decisive in completing both smaller financings and large campuses."

Write to Rob Curran at rob.curran@wsj.com
